summary: In our project, we are investigating the possibilities of data sonification that can help make complicated Earth sciences data accessible, fun, and comprehensible. Sonification refers to the technique that implies using audio other than speech in order to represent certain information. We aim to create scientific visualization that can be more accessible for people with blindness and partial loss of vision. In order to realize this, we created an interactive web-based museum, where the scientific images are displayed as digital works of art. And when clicked, you get information about it in the form of sonification. The project involves image processing with the use of HTML and JavaScript that helps to obtain data in CSV format, the sonification of the images through Python and Jupyter Notebook, and website creation through HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The uniqueness of our project lies in the innovative scientific communication technique.
details:
Scientific visualization plays a critical role in understanding our planet, and that’s why our project aims to turn visual data into sound, making it more accessible for blind and low-vision users. Moreover, it helps us understand complex earth data; we can achieve that using sonification, which is a way to use non-speech audio to convey information or perceptualize data. We designed an interactive museum-based website where the scientific images are displayed as digital works of art. The user has the opportunity to pick one of the works and to get information about it in the form of sonification.

The tools used are

· Visual Studio:

- It was used for image processing using HTML and JavaScript and turning it into a CSV file format to store the data.

- It was used in making the website using HTML, JavaScript, and CSS.

 

· Jupyter Lab: we used it for sonification, and the language used is Python.

· Excel: to preview CSV data obtained from the image processing.

We believe what makes our project creative is the way we present our data in the form of art that turns complex earth data into something easier, more accessible, and more fun to achieve. Moreover, one of the factors I and my team considered was the short time span we had to work in and still deliver a working and complete project outcome
